title: intent sync's output misdescribes its own scope, twice: a thread-scoped --to-store says the STORE was replaced, and an unscoped one says the store and extract AGREE while the store holds 0 issues and the extract 47
body:
THE DEFECT IS NOT THREE WORDING SLIPS. IT IS THAT THE CONFIRMATION LINE CARRIES
ONE HARDCODED NOUN REGARDLESS OF WHAT THE OPERATION ACTUALLY TOUCHED.

That framing is dc's, arrived at from a third instance they hit independently,
and it is stronger than the one this row was filed under: it PREDICTS the other
two forms rather than sitting beside them. The title still describes the first
two because they are what was in hand at filing time.

THREE OBSERVED FORMS, all 2026-08-24.

1. THREAD-SCOPED WRITE, WHOLE-STORE CLAIM.
   `intent sync --to-store <STID>` replaces one thread and reports
   "the store was replaced". The scope word names the store; the operation
   touched a thread.

2. AN AGREEMENT REPORT OVER A 0-VS-47 SPLIT, WHICH THEN WROTE ANYWAY.
   An unscoped `--to-store` reported the store and the extract AGREE while the
   store held 0 issues and the extract held 47. This is the expensive one: it
   cost roughly an hour of wrong attribution, because "agree" reads as evidence
   that the sync was innocent at exactly the moment the data was already gone.
   The real cause was `intent upgrade` (see 0070), and this message pointed
   away from it.

3. THE WARNING AND THE CONFIRMATION COUNT DIFFERENT THINGS (dc).
   Three issues edited in canon, unscoped `--to-store`:

       warning: replacing the store from the extract OVERWRITES:
         issue 70: differs on disk
         issue 71: differs on disk
         issue 72: differs on disk
       ok: store replaced from the extract, 58 thread(s)

   The warning names ISSUES. The ok line counts THREADS. And 58 is not a count
   of anything that changed -- it is simply how many threads exist.

WHY THE HARDCODED-NOUN READING IS THE RIGHT ONE. Under it, all three forms are
the same bug: the confirmation is written once, with a fixed noun and a fixed
population, and does not vary with the operation. Under the wording-slip
reading they are three unrelated fixes and nothing predicts the fourth.

WHAT A CORRECT CONFIRMATION OWES: the scope actually operated on, and a count of
what CHANGED rather than of what exists. A number that names the population
instead of the delta is not a confirmation, it is a coincidence that happens to
be printed after a write.

HAZARD FOR ANYONE FIXING 0070. A regression test for the issue-destroying
upgrade that asserts via sync's agreement report INHERITS this defect and will
pass over an emptied store. Assert on counts read from the store directly.
dc's repro does, which is the only reason it can see the loss.

Reported forms 1 and 2 by vc; form 3 and the hardcoded-noun generalisation by
dc, 2026-08-24 15:52Z.
